'''Materials''' are items used for [[building]] or for [[crafting]] other items.

==[[Metal]]==
===Ores===
*{{Item link|Black Metal Scrap}} – Dropped by [[Fuling]]s, [[Fuling Berserker]]s, and [[Fuling Shaman]]s.
*{{Item link|Copper Ore}} – Mined from copper veins in the [[Black Forest]].
*{{Item link|Copper Scrap}} – Destroying certain [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]] structures in the [[Mistlands]].
*{{Item link|Flametal Ore}} – Mined from [[Flametal Ore Vein]]s in the [[Ashlands]].
*{{Item link|Petrified Tissue}} – Destroying [[Petrified Gammeltroll]]s.
*{{Item link|Scrap Iron}} – Mined from [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s in the [[Swamp]]. Looted from chests in [[Sunken Crypts]]. Mined from [[Ancient Sword]]s and [[Ancient Armor]] in the [[Mistlands]].
*{{Item link|Silver Ore}} – Mined from veins in the [[Mountains]] located with the [[Wishbone]].
*{{Item link|Tin Ore}} – Mined from [[Tin Deposit]]s found near bodies of water in the [[Black Forest]], also sometimes drops from [[Black Forest|Barrels]].

===Ingots===
*{{Item link|Black Metal}} – Refined in a [[Blast Furnace]] from [[Black Metal Scrap]].
*{{Item link|Bloodgold}} – Refined in a [[Blast Furnace]] from [[Petrified Tissue]].
*{{Item link|Bronze}} – Crafted at a [[Forge]] by combining two [[Copper]] with one [[Tin]].
*{{Item link|Copper}} – Refined in a [[Smelter]] from [[Copper Ore]].
*{{Item link|Flametal}} – Refined in a [[Blast Furnace]] from [[Flametal Ore]].
*{{Item link|Iron}} – Refined in a [[Smelter]] from [[Scrap Iron]]. Looted from chests.
*{{Item link|Silver}} – Refined in a [[Smelter]] from [[Silver Ore]].
*{{Item link|Tin}} – Refined in a [[Smelter]] from [[Tin Ore]].

'''Silver Ore''' is a raw metal that can be mined from [[Silver Vein]]s found in [[Mountain]] biomes above 120 meters using an [[Iron Pickaxe]] or better. The ore can be smelted into [[Silver]] using a [[Smelter]].

== Availability ==
Silver Veins can be found using the [[Wishbone]] obtained from [[Bonemass]].

Alternatively, hitting the ground with the [[Stagbreaker]] or the [[Wooden Sledge]] may reveal underground silver deposits through the "too hard" message that appears when a silver vein is in the damage area of the two-handed club.

Trenching your positions may inadvertently reveal silver veins, provided you are above 120 meters in elevation. Despite the ground appearing frozen, it is no more difficult to dig in the Mountains than in other biomes, so hitting a vein by sheer luck is not out of the question.

== Notes ==
* Like other metals, Silver Ore cannot be teleported without a [[Portal Stone]].
* If Drakes and Obsidian (100 meters for both) are spawning near the player, they are close to the height needed (120 meters) for Silver to spawn.
* [[Cart]]s may be difficult to use in the Mountains due to the slopes but can be useful to help reduce further trips.
* Silver ore is the heaviest ore of all the ore types.
* Silver Veins cannot be mined by [[Stone Golem]]s or using an [[Antler Pickaxe]].

Bonfires are [[Player base|base]] structures used for cooking, sleeping and warmth.

Compared to [[Campfire]]s, they provide fire over a larger area and do not go out during rain.
== Notes ==
* Bonfires can only be placed on the ground and on stone structures.
* Multiple [[Cooking Station]]s can be placed around the Bonfire, however, the [[Cauldron]] does not work as it needs the fire directly underneath it.

{{image link|Wooden atgeir|size=48px}}{{image link|Wooden greatsword|size=48px}} |} == Properties== ===Wielding (One-handed/Two-handed)=== Only '''one-handed weapons''' can be simultaneously equipped with [[shields]] or a [[Torch]]. All melee '''two-handed weapons''' have a greater movement speed reduction and cannot be used together with shields or a torch. ===[[Damage and Blocking Mechanics|Offensive and defensive properties]]=== ====Damage/Damage type==== All damages in ''[[Valheim]]'' have a '''damage type'''. Some [[creatures]] have weaknesses/resistances to certain [[damage types]], which increases/decreases the effectiveness of these damages. For example, [[Skeleton]]s are weak to blunt damage and resist pierce damage. When creatures are hit by damage with damage types they are weak/resist to, the damage numbers would be shown in yellow/grey color compared to the usual white color. Similar types of weapons mostly deal the same type of damage: *Blunt damage: One/two-handed [[Clubs]] *Slash damage: One/two-handed [[Axes]], [[Swords]] *Pierce damage: [[Spears]], [[Polearms]], [[Pickaxes]], [[Bows]] *Half slash, half pierce damage: [[Knives]] Exceptions include weapons that deal elemental damage like [[Torch]], [[Frostner]] and [[Draugr fang]]. Some [[clubs]] including [[Stagbreaker]] and [[Porcupine]] also deal pierce damage besides blunt damage. Keep in mind that not all damage types are upgraded when upgrading some weapons. ====Block armor and block force==== All weapons have a value of block armor, indicating the amount of damage absorbed when blocked by the weapon. Block force shows the amount of knockback applied to enemies when blocked. ====[[Parry|Parry and Parry bonus]]==== Weapons and shields, except tower [[shields]], can be used to parry attacks, with varying parry bonuses. Parry bonus is a multiplier to block armor (damage absorbed) when parrying. Damage dealt to the enemy in a period of time after a successful parry that absorbs all the damage is always 2x. Parry bonus is mostly determined by the weapon type: *Tower [[shields]]: Cannot parry *[[Tankard]], [[Bows]], Round [[shields]]: 1.5x *Buckler [[shields]]: 2.5x *[[Polearms]] (atgeirs): 3x *[[Knives]]: 4x *[[Flesh rippers]]: 6x *All other weapons: 2x ====Backstab==== Backstab indicates the multiplier applied to enemies when backstabbing. The backstab bonus is applied when attacking unaware enemies, regardless of whether they are facing towards or away from the player. Backstabbing an enemy gives it a backstab immunity for 5 minutes. Backstabbing can occur even if the enemy has partial HP. An enemy which has a red exclamation point over its name and HP bar, indicating that it is aware of your location, cannot be backstabbed. *[[Abyssal Harpoon]]: 1x *Two-handed [[clubs]]: 2x *[[Tankard]] (Cannot attack): 4x *[[Knives]] and [[Flesh rippers]]: 6x *All other weapons, including [[bows]] and one-handed [[clubs]]: 3x ====Knockback==== Knockback shows how far enemies are knocked back when attacked by the weapon. ===Movement speed=== Most weapons, when equipped, decrease the character's movement speed and increase dodge roll cost. The movement speed effect is mostly determined by the weapon type: *[[Flesh Rippers]] and [[Knives]]: -0% (No movement speed reduction) *All other one-handed melee weapons, [[Bows]], non-Tower [[Shields]], [[Pickaxes]], [[Polearms]], and [[Magic]]: -5% *[[Serpent Scale Shield]]: -15% *Two-handed [[Axes]], two-handed [[Clubs]], and [[Shields|Tower Shields]] other than [[Serpent Scale Shield]]: -20% == Melee weapons == Melee weapons are [[items]] that can be equipped to increase attack damage. Different types of melee weapon can have different ranges, attack speeds, stamina costs per attack and secondary attacks. When equipping one-handed weapons, the character can also equip [[shields]]. Most melee weapons' attack pattern involve a 3-hit combo. Generally, the first hit has the slowest delay (from the initial click), the second hit has less delay, and the third hit is slightly slower while dealing the most damage. Most melee weapons are quicker to recover and block from a miss than after a direct strike. Below are details regarding each type of melee weapon: === [[Axes]] === Axes are the only type of weapon that can be used to cut down trees. Though they can also be used against creatures, the lower slash damage compared to [[swords]] makes this inadvisable. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Axes}} |} === [[Clubs]] === Clubs primarily deal [[Damage types|blunt]] damage and feature high knockback. The knockback from clubs allows the player to keep enemies at arms' length and is sufficient to displace some enemies out of their effective attack range. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Clubs}} |} === [[Swords]] === Swords have low knockback and low stamina cost for good damage. Sword damage is not reduced when several enemies or objects are hit by a single attack, unlike most other weapons. {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Swords}} |} === [[Spears]] === Spears have a fast attack with short range and low stamina cost. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Spears}} |} === [[Polearms]] === Polearms are strong two-handed weapons. All polearms deal pierce damage, and have a distinct AoE special attack. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Polearms}} |} === [[Knives]] === Knives have fast attacks with short range and low stamina cost. Knives deal 6x damage against unalerted enemies, whereas most other weapons do 3x. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Knives}} |} === [[Fists]] === When a player attacks without a weapon, tool equipped, or use a dedicated Fist weapon such as the [[Flesh Rippers]], they do a Fist strike. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Fists}} |} === [[Shields]] === Shields are weapons that can be used with other one-handed weapons. The block power, parry force and parry bonus of the weapons used with shields would be replaced by that of the shield used. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" !{{:Shields}} |} == Ranged weapons == === [[Bows]] === Bows are weapons that shoot equipped arrows. Unlike melee weapons, attacks consume equipped [[arrows]] and can be charged while spending stamina to increase range and damage. Bows cannot be used when there are no arrows left in the inventory. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" ! rowspan="2" |{{:Bows}} |} === [[Crossbows]] === Crossbows are weapons that shoot equipped bolts. The '''Sap Extractor''' is a structure used to harvest {{Item link|Sap}} from [[Ancient Roots]] in the [[Mistlands]] [[Biomes|biome]].

==Building==
Sap Extractors can be built on Ancient Roots within the range of a [[Workbench]].

It requires [[Black Metal]], [[Yggdrasil Wood]] and a [[Dvergr Extractor]], obtained from [[Dvergr Component Crate]]s.

==Usage==
When placed on [[Ancient Roots]], the Sap Extractor will extract {{Item link|Sap|1}} from the root every 60 seconds. It can hold a maximum of 10 Sap and glows green if it contains any Sap to harvest. As it is extracting, green particles will leave the top and bottom of the extractor. The particles will stop appearing at the top once the extractor is full, or if attempting to extract from a completely dried root.

As Ancient Roots regenerate Sap much slower than it is extracted, at 1 sap per {{duration|400}} (see their page for details). It is strategic to relocate extractors between multiple roots. Destroying or deconstructing an extractor with Sap inside does not drop the Sap.

==Tips==
* The required Black Metal cannot easily be teleported to the extraction site:
** Therefore, it is advisable to transport some by [[Boat]] before setting off to explore the Mistlands. Ideally, scout the biome for a location with many Ancient Roots as well as tillable ground in proximity, and if so, carry over the Black Metal and set up an outpost.
** Alternatively, the Mistlands biome are generally close to the [[Plains]], so it is possible to acquire [[Black Metal Scrap]] on site. The [[Iron]] needed to build a [[Blast Furnace]] can be mined from [[Ancient Sword]] or [[Ancient Armor]]. All other materials can be teleported via [[Portal]].

'''Ancient Roots''' are a resource found in the [[Mistlands]] biome. [[Sap Extractor]]s can be placed on them to harvest [[Sap]].

==Availability==
Ancient Roots can be commonly found in Mistlands, at ground level. They emit a green light glow which can be seen through the mist.

== Sap harvesting==
Each root dries up as [[Sap]] is extracted from it using a [[Sap Extractor]]. Each Sap Extractor collects and stores one sap every 60 seconds. Multiple sap extractors can be placed on one Ancient Root.

The reservoir of sap in an ancient root regenerates at a rate of 1 sap per {{duration|400}}, up to a maximum storage of 50 sap (obtained in {{duration|20000}}). Thus, sap is a renewable resource. 

Ancient Roots have three visual states: Full, half dried, and dried up.
